page_title: Rigs — virtual machines and containers on your Linux desktop
meta_description: Rigs is a fast, native Linux desktop app to start, stop and watch QEMU/KVM virtual machines, Podman and Docker containers, Compose projects and libvirt domains. Works on any desktop.
tagline: Your virtual machines and containers, at a glance
lead: Start, stop and watch QEMU/KVM machines, Podman and Docker containers, Compose projects and libvirt domains from one calm, native window.
platforms: Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and Arch Linux · any desktop · x86_64
features_title: Made for the machines you already run
f1_text: Your own QEMU scripts, single containers, Compose projects and libvirt domains share one list with the same Start, Stop and Connect buttons.
f2_text: CPU and memory for the host and every machine, plus the memory the guest itself reports, drawn as smooth sparklines.
f3_text: When something does not start, Rigs says why — a missing folder, a busy port, no KVM access — and offers a command you can copy.
f4_text: Rigs looks for existing containers and virtual machines, and reads compose.yaml or run-vm.sh to fill in the settings for you.
f5_text: Insert and eject ISO images on a running QEMU machine, without restarting it.
f6_text: Built with GTK 4 and libadwaita, it starts instantly and runs on KDE Plasma, Hyprland, Sway and others. On GNOME it feels at home and also appears in Shell search.

src_requires: Needs meson, vala, GTK 4.10+, Libadwaita 1.5+, json-glib and libsoup 3.
note_tools: Rigs manages what is already on your computer: install podman or docker, and optionally qemu, virsh, virt-viewer or remmina, from your distribution.
note_flatpak: There is no Flatpak on purpose: a sandbox cannot see the processes and sockets of your virtual machines.
note_desktops: No GNOME required: the package brings only the GTK 4 and libadwaita libraries. Outside GNOME, notifications need a notification daemon (mako, dunst, Plasma), and on Hyprland or Sway you can enable the dark style with: gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme prefer-dark
note_config: Your settings live in ~/.config/rigs/vms.json, an ordinary file you can read, edit and back up.
footer_note: Rigs is an independent project and is not affiliated with the GNOME Foundation.
